researcher_notes: Amigo LNG (LNG Alliance/Epcilon, Guaymas, Sonora) was publicly launched in 2022 (site launch ceremony April 2022) as a two-train, 7.8 MTPA export project, i.e. the second train (T2) was part of the project's original 2022 proposal. The verified 2022 source ties the 7.8 MTPA two-train plan to 2022. Single non-primary source (offshore-technology and lngprime/breakbulk pages load but did not contain a 4-digit '2022' to pass the verifier), so tier=low; year (2022 first proposal of the second train) is well-supported but not independently double-verified.

Unit 1 = NFE Fast LNG 1 (FLNG 1), the company's first Fast LNG unit (1.4 MTPA), which was deployed offshore Altamira and began operating in 2024. NFE reached its final investment decision / full notice-to-proceed on this first Fast LNG unit on 16 March 2021 (NTP to Fluor/Chart/Baker Hughes); the verified source documents the 2021 FID. Caveat: at the March 2021 FID the deployment site was not yet publicly fixed to Altamira; the Altamira-site commitment came via NFE's finalized CFE agreements on 28 Oct 2022 (businesswire/IR releases bot-blocked, could not verify). If GEM intends the FID milestone to mean the Altamira-site sanction rather than the unit build-FID, the year would be 2022. Reported 2021 as the actual build-FID of the unit; tier=low because the verified source does not name 'Altamira' (the unit was unnamed-site at FID).

Unit 2 = NFE's second Altamira FLNG unit (FLNG 2 / onshore Train 2, developed with CFE on the existing Altamira terminal infrastructure). NFE sanctioned the second unit in July 2024 with the closing of a $700 million loan that fully funds its construction (de facto FID; NFE does not issue a formal 'FID' label). Year 2024 corroborated by three independent publishers (GIIGNL news, Yahoo/Zacks, Mexico Business News). Construction/COD subsequently slipped to 2026-2027, but the investment-decision year is 2024.

Could not verify a specific cancellation year from independent sources. Progreso LNG (Kogas import-terminal MOU with Yucatan, 2016) saw no development after 2016; a Milenio report (8 Jan 2020, 'En Progreso no cabe terminal gasera') noted the Port of Progreso lacks space for an international-standard LNG terminal, and the project is GEM-inferred cancelled (~2020, i.e. last activity 2016 + 4 y). No independent source explicitly states a cancellation year, and I could not retrieve a citable Milenio URL, so left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate a link. Best estimate if forced: 2020.

Trains 4-6 are the expansion (Phase 2) added when Mexico Pacific doubled the Saguaro Energia project to six ~4.7-MTPA trains (~28.2 MTPA) in January 2022, the year the trains 4-6 expansion was first publicly proposed. Verified one independent media source containing 2022 + Saguaro + 'six'. Could not double-verify (NaturalGasIntel glossary 403/Cloudflare; pgjonline did not contain the tokens), so tier=low. The six-train plan was later trimmed (downsized to 3 trains, court docs July 2025), but the proposal of trains 4-6 dates to 2022.

Could not verify a specific shelving year from independent sources. The CFE-led Salina Cruz LNG export concept was revived/proposed by the Mexican government in October 2020 (3 MTPA, fed via the Jaltipan-Salina Cruz pipeline expansion); analysts deemed it unfeasible, and it has had no substantive news since, so it is GEM-inferred shelved (no activity 2+ years). No independent source labels or dates the shelving (the inferred milestone year would be ~2023, i.e. last activity ~2021 + 2 y), so left UNRESOLVED rather than cite an unsupported year.

Could not verify a cancellation year. Multiple distinct Dongying (Shandong) LNG records exist (China Huadian 2014 proposal, Hainuo Port, and an FSRU variant); I could not isolate Chinese-language sourcing for the specific 'Dongying FSRU' project, and no independent source states a cancellation year (GEM-inferred cancelled, ~last activity + 4 y). Left UNRESOLVED rather than cite the wrong Dongying project or fabricate a year.

The Zhongtian Energy (中天能源) Jiangyin (江阴) inland LNG terminal, built via subsidiary Jiangsu Honghai (江苏鸿海/泓海), stalled when construction halted (~2019, ~99% complete by April 2021) and the sponsor collapsed: parent Zhongtian Energy was delisted in 2022 and the project subsidiary entered bankruptcy reorganization (Jiangyin court accepted the case 8 Nov 2022). I report 2022 as the de facto shelving year (the year of the definitive collapse), verified on a 2022 source (Sohu) with a 2023 Sina Finance source corroborating the bankruptcy context. Tier=low: the milestone year is an interpretation (sources document the 2022 collapse but do not label it 'shelved'); GEM 'inferred 2 y' could place it at 2021 (halt ~2019) or 2023 depending on the last-activity basis.

Could not verify a shelving year. PetroChina's Jieyang (揭阳, Guangdong) LNG terminal Phase 1 (3 MTPA) was promoted in Jieyang's 14th Five-Year Plan (2021) with a target trial-operation by 2025; progress reported slow as of late 2020, but no independent source labels or dates a shelving (GEM-inferred shelved, ~last activity + 2 y). Left UNRESOLVED rather than cite an unsupported year.

Could not verify a shelving year. The Jiujiang (九江, Jiangxi) inland-river LNG terminal was a feasibility-stage proposal (one of the Yangtze inland LNG terminals in the Ministry of Transport layout plan) with no progress reported after ~2021; it is GEM-inferred shelved. No independent source labels or dates the shelving (inferred milestone ~2022-2023), so left UNRESOLVED.

Could not verify a cancellation year. Same Jiujiang (九江, Jiangxi) inland LNG terminal as st_id 2631; after the feasibility-stage proposal went dormant (no news after ~2021-2024), it is GEM-inferred cancelled (~last activity + 4 y, i.e. ~2024-2025). No independent source labels or dates a cancellation, so left UNRESOLVED.
